extracted.intended_audience: medical communicators, authors, medical writers, editors submitting to or preparing manuscripts for medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding who qualifies as an author versus a non-author contributor on medical journal manuscripts, plus how to acknowledge contributors (including professional medical writers and AI use). Targets people preparing or managing manuscript bylines and acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICMJE four authorship criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: “Substantial contributions to the conception or design of the work; or the acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of data for the work; AND Drafting the work or reviewing it critically for important intellectual content; AND Final approval of the version to be published; AND Agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work in ensuring that questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are appropriately investigated and resolved.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals who meet all of these criteria should be identified as authors. If they don’t meet these criteria, they should be acknowledged as non-author contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship confers credit and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship byline signifies that authors are taking responsibility for the content and confers credit with important academic, social, and financial implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because authors are accountable, accurate assignment of authorship affects academic credit and ethical responsibility for the integrity of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author group decides authorship and order
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICMJE’s guidelines make it clear that authors and collaborators are responsible for deciding who meets the criteria for authorship; not journal editors. The author group also decides the order in which the authors are listed on the byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve authorship membership and order within the collaborating team rather than expecting editors to adjudicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for adding/removing authors after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors request removal or addition of an author after manuscript submission or publication, journal editors should seek an explanation and signed statement of agreement for the requested change from all listed authors and from the author to be removed or added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect signed agreement and an explanation from everyone involved before editors enact post-submission changes to the author list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author is designated to communicate with the journal editor during submission, peer review, and publication and needs to be available and accessible to fulfill administrative duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author should share authorship details, provide additional information, answer queries or pass them along to coauthors, and ensure all listed authors receive copies of correspondence from editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for acknowledging non-author contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: When someone contributes to a manuscript but does not meet the 4 criteria for authorship, they should still receive recognition. Examples include acquiring funding, supervision of a research group or general administrative support, writing assistance, technical or language editing, and proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge contributors individually or under a heading like 'Clinical Investigators' or 'Participating Investigators.' Corresponding author should obtain written permission from individuals before acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify contributor roles in acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators' contributions should be specifically identified using phrases such as 'Served as scientific advisors', 'Critically reviewed the study proposal', 'Collected data', 'Provided and cared for study patients', 'Participated in writing or technical editing of the manuscript'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, specific language to describe each contributor's role rather than vague or generic statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of AI writing assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If artificial intelligence (AI) is used for writing assistance, this should be indicated in the acknowledgement section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many prominent science and health publications don’t allow AI to be named as an author; authors and medical writers remain responsible for the content created with AI and must disclose its use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging professional medical writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who collaborate with medical writers should acknowledge any writing support received and include the name and qualifications of the writer, that person's specific contributions, and any funding source used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example disclosure: 'The authors thank [name and qualifications] of [company, city, country] for providing medical writing support/editorial support [specify and/or expand as appropriate], which was funded by [sponsor, city, country] in accordance with Good Publication Practice 2022 guidelines.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional medical writers who meet authorship criteria should be coauthors
rubrics_metrics.description: The joint position statement from AMWA/EMWA/ISMPP indicates that professional medical writers who meet the ICMJE authorship criteria should be recognized as coauthors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a medical writer satisfies all four ICMJE authorship criteria, list them as an author rather than only in acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to follow journal-specific instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICMJE guidelines are crafted for ICMJE member journals but many non-ICMJE journals have adopted similar guidelines; the ICMJE recommends that authors consult its guidelines while also following individual journals' instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ICMJE as a baseline but always check and comply with the target journal’s specific authorship and acknowledgement policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and transparent reporting through correct attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Following ICMJE authorship guidelines and properly disclosing contributors and medical communicators ensures a transparent and ethical process for publishing research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical writers and editors play an important role helping authors share research accurately and timely; correct attribution supports research integrity and patient-care advancement.
